question: Who launched India's first 'One Health Consortium’?

options.text: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Science and Technology**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's first '**One Health Consortium**' was launched by the **Ministry of Science and Technology**.
 
• The initiative aims to address health issues through an integrated approach encompassing human, animal, and environmental health.
 
• The consortium will work on monitoring and controlling zoonotic diseases, which are diseases that can be transmitted from animals to humans.
 
• This integrated approach is crucial for early detection and prevention of potential pandemics.
 
• It is a collaborative effort involving multiple stakeholders including various research institutions, government bodies, and international organizations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The 'One Health' concept recognizes that the health of people is closely connected to the health of animals and our shared environment.
 
• The Ministry of Science and Technology focuses on promoting scientific research and innovation in various fields, including health.
 
• In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, the importance of a 'One Health' approach has been increasingly recognized globally.
 
• India has been proactive in adopting this approach to safeguard public health and to ensure a sustainable and healthy future.
 
• The consortium will also focus on capacity building and training of professionals in the 'One Health' approach to strengthen the overall healthcare system.
